title.narrative: Gendered Violence and Poor Mental Health of Migrants in Precarious Situations (GEMMS)

description.narrative: GEMMS is a multi-country global health research programme on gendered violence, poor mental health, and precarity among migrants in precarious situations. The programme is led by the University of Essex and works across India, Cambodia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe, with direct implementing partners including the University of Witwatersrand, Tata Institute for Social Sciences, Health Poverty Action (Cambodia), Health Poverty Action (Zimbabwe), the University of Oxford, and the University of Essex.

Planned activities include contextual and situational analysis; scoping reviews of relevant literature and intervention or service delivery approaches; identification and appraisal of existing data sources; key informant interviews; local stakeholder meetings; development and refinement of research questions and tools; quantitative surveys; longitudinal phone tracing; in-depth qualitative interviews; participatory workshops using methods such as photovoice and resource mapping; collaborative analysis workshops; scoping review of mental health and gender-based violence policies; co-design of locally applicable actions and interventions; piloting of interventions; and dissemination, public engagement, and policy dialogue events. Data collection activities are planned for India, Cambodia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe. Literature reviews and evidence appraisals are planned across all four country sites as well as the University of Essex and the University of Oxford.
Target groups include migrants in precarious situations, health workers, and service providers in India, Cambodia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.

Workstream 1 (Evidence) evaluates existing evidence and service gaps to inform the design of research and intervention tools. It addresses the existing evidence on intersecting risks of gendered violence and poor mental health among migrants in precarious situations in the four countries, tools to capture these risks over time and place, and current services and approaches that address gendered violence and mental health in the research sites and their responsiveness to migrant needs.

Workstream 2 (Experience) conducts research with migrants in precarious situations, health workers, and service providers to generate new knowledge on the burden and lived experiences of intersecting risks for gendered violence and poor mental health, and on the socio-economic determinants and contextual mechanisms that shape risk distribution and access to resources that can reduce gendered violence and enhance mental health.

Workstream 3 (Intervention) draws on the new knowledge generated to develop a participatory approach to co-design actions to interrupt the cycle of gendered violence and poor mental health among migrants in precarious situations, alongside a training and support intervention for healthcare workers and service providers.
